decisions.reason: As a flagship digital extension tightly linked to the core practice software and to the firm's direction toward connected workflows, it still has high strategic option value and is worth keeping.
The education institute is adjacent to the firm's existing support and training capabilities, so it is relatively inexpensive to maintain while preserving customer ties and learning value.
A remote support tool complements the installed software base and can lower service frictions, so the firm would likely keep this low-cost option open unless usage is clearly weak.
Practice analytics fits the firm's core software and the broader move toward data-driven management, so its upside remains attractive relative to the cost of staying in the market.
A complete practice bundle is strongly aligned with the firm's core offer and customer segments, and as a bundled proposition it is cheap to continue and commercially useful.

The job and practice portal is the most peripheral and likely requires different network economics from the core software business, so after several years the firm would be inclined to redeploy resources elsewhere.
